paragraphs.en: {Dogs} {greet} each other nose-first, as it were— {sniffing} each other from {fore} to {aft} .People are not quite so open about the process of sniffing each other out.But the {size} of the {perfume} {industry} suggests {scent} is important in human {relations} , too.There is also {evidence} that human {beings} can {infer} kinship ( (亲戚关系) ), {deduce} emotional states and even {detect} disease {via} the sense of smell.
paragraphs.cn: 可以说， <u> 狗 </u> 会先用鼻子互相 <u> 打招呼 </u> ——从 <u> 前 </u> 到 <u> 后 </u> 地把对方 <u> 闻 </u> 一遍。而人类在相互了解彼此的过程中可不会这么直白。不过， <u> 香水产业 </u> 的 <u> 规模 </u> 却表明， <u> 气味 </u> 在人际 <u> 关系 </u> 中也很重要。还有 <u> 证据 </u> 表明， <u> 人类 </u> 可以 <u> 通过 </u> 嗅觉 <u> 推断 </u> 亲缘关系， <u> 推测 </u> 情绪状态，甚至 <u> 检测 </u> 出疾病。

paragraphs.en: Now, researchers from the Weizmann {Institute} of Science in Israel have gone a step further.They think they have shown, {admittedly} in a {fairly} small {sample} of individuals, that friends actually smell {alike} .They have also shown that this is probably the case from the beginning, with people picking friends at least {partly} on the {basis} of body odor ( (气味) ), rather than the body odors of people who become friends {subsequently} converging ( (趋同) ).
paragraphs.cn: 现在，以色列魏茨曼科学 <u> 研究院 </u> 的研究者已经又向前迈进了一步。他们认为自己的研究已经说明，能做朋友的人确实闻起来 <u> 很像 </u> —— <u> 当然 </u> ，研究的 <u> 样本 </u> 仅包括 <u> 相当 </u> 少数的个体。他们还证明，这种情况很可能从一开始就是如此。也就是说，至少 <u> 在一定程度上 </u> ，人们是 <u> 根据 </u> 气味来挑选朋友的，而不是在朋友关系建立 <u> 之后 </u> ，气味才逐渐趋同。

paragraphs.en: They started their research by testing the odors of 20 {pairs} of same-sex friends who were not in a {romantic} relationship.They did this using an {electronic} {nose} and also two groups of specially employed human “smellers”.The e-nose employed a set of {gas} {sensors} to {assess T-shirts worn} by participants.One group of human smellers were given pairs of these shirts and asked to {rate} how similar they smelt.Those in the other group were asked to rate the odors of individual T-shirts on five {subjective} {dimensions} : {pleasantness} , {intensity} , {attractiveness} , {competence} and warmth.All three approaches {yielded} the same result.The T-shirts of friends smelt more similar to each other than the T-shirts of {strangers} .Friends, in other words, do {indeed} smell alike.
paragraphs.cn: 他们首先对20 <u> 对 </u> 处于非 <u> 恋爱 </u> 关系的同性朋友身上的气味进行了测试。他们使用了一个 <u> 电子鼻 </u> ，以及两组专门雇用的人类“嗅探员”来进行测试。电子鼻使用一组 <u> 气体传感器 </u> 来 <u> 评估 </u> 参与者 <u> 穿 </u> 过的 <u> T恤衫 </u> 。一组人类“嗅探员”拿到成对的T恤衫，并按要求 <u> 评定 </u> 它们的气味相似程度。另一组人则被要求通过五个 <u> 主观维度 </u> 对单件T恤衫的气味进行评分，包括 <u> 愉悦度 </u> 、 <u> 浓烈程度 </u> 、 <u> 吸引力 </u> 、 <u> 能力 </u> 和温暖感。这三种测试方法都 <u> 得出 </u> 了相同的结果。与 <u> 陌生人 </u> 的T恤衫相比，朋友的T恤衫闻起来更相似。换句话说，朋友之间 <u> 确实 </u> 有类似的气味。

paragraphs.en: Why scent might play a role in forming friendships remains obscure.Other qualities related to being friends, including age, appearance, education, {religion} and race, are either immediately obvious or rapidly become so.But while some individuals have strong and {noticeable} body odor, many—at least since the use of {soap} has become {widespread} —do not.It is {present} .But it is {subconscious} .
paragraphs.cn: 气味为何可以在友谊的形成过程中发挥作用仍不得而知。与成为朋友相关的其他特质，包括年龄、外貌、受教育程度、 <u> 宗教信仰 </u> 和种族，要么是一目了然，要么很快就能知晓。然而，尽管有些人有强烈而 <u> 明显的 </u> 体味，但许多人——至少自从 <u> 肥皂广泛 </u> 使用以来——并非如此。体味是 <u> 存在的 </u> ，不过它是 <u> 潜意识的 </u> 。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
